ByteSize.description: A byte size: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `b`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, or `tb`; units are binary, so `1kb` is 1024 bytes.

ChangedPaths.description: Whether the changed project paths ride the hook's command line.

oneOf.description: The command runs exactly as configured.

The changed project paths follow the configured `arguments`, in byte
order, for a tool that takes files.

CommandHook.description:
One `[[hooks]]` block: an executable Rift starts directly — no shell —
inside the changed tree each time a change applies. Every key is
required; the schema carries no defaults.

arguments.description: The program's literal arguments, in order. May be empty.

changed_paths.description:
Whether the changed project paths are appended after `arguments` in
byte order.

determinism.description:
Whether an identical tree and environment are expected to reproduce
the result.

environment.description:
Environment values added on top of the environment the server
inherited.

guarantees.description:
What a passing run establishes. Each entry becomes evidence on the
change the hook checked.

id.description: Label for this hook's results, unique within the list.

kind.description: What the hook is: a test suite, a linter, a build, or something else.

output_limit_bytes.description:
Bytes of each output stream Rift keeps, 256 to 4096. The full size
is still reported.

program.description:
The executable Rift starts. An absolute path is refused; a bare name
resolves through `PATH`, a relative one below `working_directory`.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds before Rift kills the process, 1 to 3600000.

type.description: How the hook runs; `command` is the only type.

working_directory.description:
Directory the process starts in, relative to the changed tree's
root. Empty selects the root.

oneOf.description: Every visible file of the workspace.
The workspace, its dependencies, and the standard library together.

CoverageScope.description:
What a completeness statement covers — everything the request asked for, one file, or a
standing scope the answer holds over.

oneOf.description: A standing scope identified by its name.
A single unit is just a file: the claim holds for that path and says nothing about any other.

unit.description: The file the claim is about.

Determinism.description:
Whether an identical tree and environment are expected to reproduce a
hook's result.

oneOf.description: The same tree and environment give the same answer.
The result may vary between identical runs.

Duration.description: A duration: an integer magnitude with a required unit suffix `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`.

ExecutionConfiguration.description:
The `[execution]` table. `execute` stays off until `allow` names the
languages caller-provided code may run as.

allow.description:
Language selectors enabled for `execute`: a language name, or
`name:dialect` to pin a dialect. Empty keeps execution off.

max_code.description: Bytes one submitted block may hold, 1b to 32kb.

max_concurrent.description: Evaluations running at once across the whole workspace.

max_output.description: Bytes each captured stream keeps, up to 16kb.

FileId.description:
Identity of one file in the tree a request targets. The path after `rift://file/` is a
`ProjectPath` in canonical percent-encoding. The server re-validates the decoded path
wherever a `FileId` arrives, so the `ProjectPath` exclusions hold for every consumer,
whatever schema its implementation generated from.

GuaranteeKind.description: A property a verifier can establish about an applied change.

oneOf.description: Names still resolve to what they resolved to before the change.
References to the changed declarations were updated with them.
The change's behavior was exercised, such as by a test suite.

HistoryConfiguration.description:
The `[providers.history]` table. The history provider's cost scales with
how far back it walks, so its depth is the budget worth setting.

enabled.description: Whether the history provider runs at all.

max_revisions.description: Revisions the walk covers from the current head, newest first.

HookGuarantee.description: What a passing run of one hook establishes about the change it checked.

detail.description: The exact property the hook checks, and the limits on reading a pass.

HookKind.description: What a hook is, as workspace configuration presents it.

oneOf.description: A hook none of the other kinds describe.

HookType.description:
How a hook runs; `command` — an executable started directly, without a
shell — is the only type.

oneOf.description: An executable Rift starts directly inside the changed tree.

PathPattern.description:
Project-relative glob using *, ?, **, and character classes. Forward-slash separated on
every platform, whatever separator the host OS uses natively.

ProjectPath.description:
One path below the workspace root, using forward slashes and UTF-8 in Unicode NFC — Rift
normalizes what it emits and what it accepts, and compares byte-for-byte. The empty path
names the root itself. Absolute paths, backslashes, control characters, empty segments,
and `.` or `..` segments are refused before the filesystem is touched. The limit is 1000
UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A workspace holding two entries whose NFC forms are equal
fails the read that touches them with `content_unavailable`.

ProvidersConfiguration.description:
The `[providers]` table: the built-in providers run without
configuration, and this table bounds or disables them.

SearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search]` table. Search runs on a lexical index with nothing to
configure; `embedding` names the model that adds dense ranking on top,
and `text` admits non-source text files into that lexical index.

embedding.description:
The embedding model identifier. Vectors are stored per model, so
changing the value rebuilds the dense index; absent keeps search
lexical.

text.description:
Which non-source text files join the lexical index alongside code
symbols.

ServerConfiguration.description:
The `[server]` table. Filesystem scans and parses run on a bounded
blocking pool; this table sizes the pool and bounds the queue wait.
The server reads the table at startup, so a change applies on the
next start.

blocking_queue_timeout.description: Wall-clock bound one request waits for a blocking slot, 1ms to 1h.

blocking_slots.description: Blocking filesystem and parser operations running at once, 1 to 64.

SourceConfiguration.description:
The `[source]` table: which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider
visible. `.git`, `.rift`, and `target` stay invisible whatever this table says.

exclude.description:
Exact file paths or globs dropped from visibility, in [`PathPattern`] syntax. A match
here is dropped even when `include` also matches it.

include.description:
Exact file paths or globs a file must match to stay visible, in [`PathPattern`] syntax.
Empty admits every file `exclude` and `.gitignore` leave standing.

respect_gitignore.description:
Whether the workspace's own `.gitignore` files, root and nested, hide the paths they
match. Global and parent-directory gitignore sources are never read.

TextSearchConfiguration.description:
The `[search.text]` table: which non-source text files join the lexical index, as one
unit each, or as several size-bounded chunks when a file exceeds `max_chunk`.

extensions.description:
File extensions, without the leading dot, admitted as text-file lexical units:
lowercase ASCII alphanumeric only (so a leading dot is already excluded), at most
16 bytes each, at most 32 entries, no duplicates.

max_chunk.description:
Bytes one lexical chunk may hold, 1kb to 16mb. A text file larger than this is
indexed as several chunks of at most this size; an operator who wants a file out of
the index excludes it in `[source]` or drops its extension from `extensions`.

description:
The whole `rift.toml`. Every table is optional and defaults to the
behavior documented on it; any key outside these definitions refuses the
file as `configuration_invalid`.

execution.description: Enablement and limits for caller-provided code.

hooks.description:
Hooks run in the changed tree, in list order, each time a change
applies.

providers.description: Bounds and switches for the built-in providers.

search.description: The embedding model that adds dense ranking to lexical search.

server.description: The server's own blocking-work bounds: pool size and queue wait.

source.description: Which files below the workspace root the index and reads consider visible.
